site_name: CloudHQ LC campus, LC1A/LC1B/LC2/LC3, 21955 Loudoun County Parkway, Ashburn, VA
verification: All citations are directories (datacentermap, Baxtel), which are not evidence; the researcher's own notes show the directories disagree (2018 vs 2019 for LC1A). CloudHQ's LC Campus page has no opening or delivery date for the first building; its only status line is that LC3 and LC4 are under construction, on an undated page. No CloudHQ press or news page about LC1 was reachable from the site. Nothing opened supports 2018. Side note outside this task: cloudhq.com/resources/ hosts an E3 whitepaper commissioned by CloudHQ, "Beyond the Headlines: An Empirical Analysis of Data Center Impacts on Electricity Bills" (https://cloudhq.com/wp-content/uploads/e3_cloudhq.pdf); I did not open it, but it may belong in the study's prior-work list as industry-funded work.

lead.year_evidence_quote: The data center entered service in 2018 with its first phase (LC1A)
lead.notes: Datacentermap reports LC1A entered service in 2018, though Baxtel lists 2019 build year. LC1B date conflicts between 2020 and 2022. LC2 dates conflict between 2019 and 2023. Address matches LC1A/LC1B at 21955 Loudoun County Parkway per permit companies.

site_name: CoreSite VA1, 12100 Sunrise Valley Drive, Reston, VA
verification: The only cited URL is baxtel.com (directory, not evidence, not opened); the basis label assessor_year_built is wrong because no assessor record was cited. CoreSite's own pages and the market brochure (PDF text extracted) state no opening, build or acquisition year for VA1; the only date is a market-level statement that CoreSite has operated in Northern Virginia since 2007, which is not a VA1 opening date. Wikipedia's CoreSite page does not mention VA1; it records a $60 million purchase of the 22-acre Sunrise Technology Park announced in August 2016 (expansion land), which conflicts with the researcher's note that CoreSite acquired Sunrise Technology Park in 2008. A 2006 'year built' may also describe the building shell rather than first data center operation (inference). A Fairfax County assessment record or CoreSite SEC filing would be the place to settle it.

lead.notes: Baxtel lists 2006 build year. Building was previously Sunrise Technology Park used by America Online before CoreSite acquired it in 2008. Could not find CoreSite opening announcement, so using assessor-style year built from directory.

site_name: Digital Realty ACC2 (former DuPont Fabros), 44490 Chillum Place, Ashburn, VA
year_evidence_quote: In the first quarter of 2005, we began developing the infrastructure of ACC2, and in October 2005 we completed development and brought the property into service as a wholesale data center.
year_site_match: DuPont Fabros IPO prospectus (SEC, p. 87) puts ACC2 and ACC3 on the same 22 acres at Ashburn Corporate Center Phase I Condominium, Loudoun County; the permit holder is DuPont Fabros Technology, and Digital Realty's Northern Virginia page lists ex-DuPont Fabros ACC6 on the same street (44461 Chilum Place). The filing does not print the street address 44490 Chillum Place; that ACC2 is the building at that number is my inference, not on a page I opened. If the address were ACC3 instead, the first building on the shared site is still ACC2.
verification: Page supports 2005, NOT the researcher's 2001. The researcher's source (DataCenterHawk) is a directory. The operator's own SEC prospectus (424B4 filed 2007-10-19) says land was acquired in 2000 and ACC2 was developed 'as an empty shell'; 'The shell was leased from mid-2001 through late 2003 to a provider of colocation services. Thereafter, ACC2 was vacant.' Infrastructure development began Q1 2005 and the building entered service as a wholesale data center in October 2005. The FY2007 10-K table shows 'Year Built/Renovated 2001/2005', which is where the 2001 figure originates. Residual uncertainty, hence medium not high: (1) the filing does not say whether the 2001-2003 colocation tenant ever ran equipment in the shell, so a small pre-2005 load cannot be ruled out; (2) the street number is not on the page. ACC3 on the same site entered service June 2006. Quote was read through WebFetch's summarizer, which returned it in two fragments that I joined; wording should be rechecked against p. 87 before publication.

lead.year_evidence_quote: The company opened its first facility, designated as ACC2, on the campus in 2001, with completed the build out by 2005.
lead.notes: DuPont Fabros opened ACC2 in 2001 and completed buildout by 2005. Digital Realty acquired the DuPont Fabros portfolio in September 2017. Address confirmed as 44490 Chillum Place per permit company.

site_name: Equinix DC10, 21551 Beaumeade Circle, Ashburn, VA
verification: The cited Equinix release is real and dated February 15, 2012, and the researcher's quote is verbatim. But both DC10 statements are forward-looking: 'This month Equinix will open DC10' and 'Phase one of DC10 ... is scheduled to open next month.' Under the rubric 'will open' is not enough, even when the horizon is days. I looked for a second Equinix page to bracket it: the Q1 2012 results release (April 25, 2012) and the May 2, 2013 DC11 launch release do not mention DC10, and no 2012 release title from February through July refers to a DC10 opening. Two gaps therefore remain: no page stating DC10 actually opened, and no opened page tying DC10 to 21551 Beaumeade Circle. 2012 is very likely correct (my judgment, not verified); an Equinix 10-K for 2012 or the DC10 facility page would close it.

lead.year_evidence_quote: This month Equinix will open DC10, the company's first Business Suites site in North America.
lead.notes: Equinix press release dated February 15, 2012 states DC10 would open that month (February 2012), though also mentions phase one scheduled to open next month. Address confirmed at 21551 Beaumeade Circle.
